items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: There was one girl especially. Her name was Lydia. I just didn't want... For some reason, I didn't want her to know no more about music than I did.

ctx.x: So he didn't have nothing to do but teach the band. So he wanted to get involved with something else. So he went around to different classes to see who would want to get in and do a class of music, public school music. So when he came to my class, I raised my hand. Because see, I had had...

I forgot to tell this about my early years of school in Muskogee. We had a teacher. I don't know where she come from. Her name was Mrs. Clark. And she taught us... She taught us so many... I mean, we were just young kids. Man, she was teaching the theory of music. And the reason... That's the only reason I learned as much as I did about music. There was one girl especially. Her name was Lydia. I just didn't want... For some reason, I didn't want her to know no more about music than I did. And I didn't study
